one_liner: Senior Executive Service job running the federal panel that resolves bargaining deadlocks between federal agencies and unions, managing staff, cases, budget and stakeholder relations.
fit_summary: This is an SES role requiring demonstrated executive leadership plus deep labor-management relations and dispute-resolution expertise (mediation, arbitration, adjudication), none of which is on file for Daniel. Daniel's policy knowledge and stakeholder skills are relevant, but emergency-management consulting is unlikely to satisfy the Technical Qualifications or the five ECQs. Apply only if your IEM work included senior leadership and genuine labor or employment dispute work.
eligibility: Open to the public, including applicants with no prior federal service; hiring paths include public and SES, and no clearance is required.

You must show both Technical Qualifications in your resume: TQ 1, dispute-resolution techniques for labor or employment disputes, and TQ 2, expertise in labor-management relations and/or employment matters.
You must show all five Executive Core Qualifications in the resume itself; separate narratives are not accepted, and OPM's QRB must certify you before appointment.
The resume is strictly limited to 2 pages, 10pt Arial or Times New Roman, with 1-inch margins, or you are immediately ineligible.
If selected, you would serve a one-year SES probationary period.
strategy: First, honestly check whether you have concrete labor or employment dispute-resolution experience; if you lack it, put your effort into better-matched roles, such as GS emergency management, FEMA, or legislative or policy positions.

If you apply, structure the 2-page resume so each ECQ and TQ is visibly evidenced with brief Challenge-Context-Action-Result accomplishments, and use OPM's SES qualifications guide Appendix 2 as a checklist.

Frame IEM work around executive-level elements only where true, such as leading teams, managing budgets, and advising government client leadership, and quantify scope with staff size, dollars, and number of clients.
Use your knowledge of American government and the Constitution to address ECQ 1, and your relationship-building to address stakeholder representation with agencies, unions, and FMCS.
Verify the formatting exactly before submitting, and apply well before the November 30, 2026 close.
resume_bullets: Led [number]-person team at IEM delivering [type of emergency management/recovery program] for [government client], managing a $[budget] budget and [result, e.g., on-time delivery or cost savings].
Facilitated negotiations among [federal/state/local agencies or stakeholder groups] to resolve [specific dispute or competing priorities], producing [agreement or outcome].
Analyzed [program metrics or case data] to recommend [process change], which [measured efficiency gain] for [client].
interview_questions: Describe a labor or employment dispute you helped resolve, including the method you used and the outcome.
How would you manage the Panel's case intake and decide which resolution procedure fits a given impasse?
Tell us about a time you cut waste or improved efficiency in an organization you led.
How have you held staff accountable while leading them through change?
watch_outs: The TQs require labor-relations and dispute-resolution expertise that is not in your known background, so you will likely be screened out without it.
SES-level executive experience is expected, and QRB certification is a demanding extra hurdle.
Any formatting violation on the 2-page resume results in automatic disqualification.
The role is based in Washington, DC and is telework-eligible but not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas.
